WIDA-ACCESS Student Growth in 2021
An Update to the New Hampshire TAC
 Damian Betebenner
 Center for Assessment

 New Hampshire TAC
 August 10th, 2021

Background
• The Center for Assessment has calculated student growth percentiles and
 student growth targets for WIDA-ACCESS in New Hampshire since 2018.
• Due to small numbers of students taking WIDA-ACCESS in middle and high
 school grades, analyses performed have been both cohort and baseline
 referenced.
• Baseline SGP growth norms were based upon multi-state WIDA-ACCESS data.
• New Hampshire accountability uses student growth targets to determine
 whether students are on track to reach English Language Proficiency (WIDA-
 ACCESS Level 4.5) within 5 years.
• The Center for Assessment currently works with 8 states on calculating growth
 for WIDA-ACCESS assessments.

Student Growth Calculations in 2020
• Unlike New Hampshire’s state summative SAS assessment, WIDA-
 ACCESS was administered in late winter 2020 before the onset of the
 COVID-19 pandemic.
• States received accountability waivers due to the suspension of state
 summative testing. Accountability waivers applied to ELP results as
 well.
• Growth analyses were conducted as usual in August 2020.

Student Growth Calculations in 2021
• WIDA-ACCESS administration occurred in later winter 2021.
• Due to the pandemic, states received accountability waivers for 2020-2021.
• New Hampshire intends to go forward with the calculation of growth as it
 normally would.
• Because the administration of WIDA-ACCESS has been without interruption
 across years and no evidence has thus far emerged of testing anomalies in
 2021 Methods of analysis will be consistent with previous years.
• However, due to the pandemic, New Hampshire may want to consider
 supplemental analyses with their data beyond normal accountability metrics.

Baseline SGP growth norms
• There are numerous indications that student learning was impeded due to
 numerous factors associated with the pandemic including:
 • Remote education for some or all of the previous year.
 • Socio-emotional, financial, or physical impacts due to the pandemic on students,
 families, and schools.
• One benefit of baseline growth norms is that the immediately allow the state
 to see to what extent student learning has slowed over the last year.
• Historical (i.e., 2020 median SGPs) will be close to 50. Decreases observed in
 2021 will, in general, be an indication on how much learning has slowed
 leading to achievement decreases.
• These decreases will, in turn, lead to higher targets.

Summary of Results
• Initial SGP growth analyses of WIDA-ACCESS data indicates larger
 impacts for elementary grade students, moderate impacts for middle
 school students, and minor to no impact for high school students.
• These results are consistent with what has been observed in other
 states.
• Though not analyzed here, presentation at NCSA by WIDA suggest
 drops in achievement are driven by scores on the speaking portion of
 the test.
